subject: physics
title: Specific Heat and Latent Heat
welcome_lead: Heat a kettle, melt some ice — quantify both with Q = m c ΔT and Q = m L.
meta_desc: A-Level Thermal Physics adventure on specific heat capacity and latent heat.
final_note: Heating a phase change costs energy with no temperature rise.

concepts.def: Energy transferred due to temperature difference.
Energy per kg per K: c = Q / (mΔT).
Heat to change temperature of mass m.
Energy for phase change at fixed T.

walkthroughs.body_html: To raise temperature of mass m by ΔT, supply Q = m c ΔT. Water has high c ≈ 4180 J/(kg·K) — that's why it makes a great coolant.
At melting and boiling points, energy goes into breaking bonds, not raising T. Q = m L where L is specific latent heat. L_v > L_f usually because more bonds break.
Heating ice at -10 °C to steam: warm ice (m c_ice ΔT) + melt (m L_f) + warm water + vaporise (m L_v) + warm steam. Sum the stages.

mcqs.q: What does specific latent heat measure?
options: The energy required to change the state of 1 kg of a substance without changing its temperature.
The temperature at which a substance melts or boils.
The energy required to raise the temperature of 1 kg by 1 degree.
Metal heats up faster because it has more thermal energy to begin with.

mcqs.q: Why does a metal spoon in hot water heat up faster than a wooden one?
options: Metal heats up faster because it has more thermal energy to begin with.
Metal heats up faster because it has a lower specific heat capacity, requiring less energy per degree.
Heat is measured in degrees Celsius and temperature in Joules.
Metals have higher thermal conductivity, so heat is transferred more rapidly through them.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between heat and temperature?
options: Metal heats up faster because it has more thermal energy to begin with.
Heat and temperature are the same thing — both measure how hot something is.
Heat is measured in degrees Celsius and temperature in Joules.
Heat is the energy transferred due to temperature difference; temperature measures average kinetic energy of particles.
